'''John Hegarty''' (born 1948) is an Irish physicist and academic who served as the 43rd [[Provost of Trinity College Dublin]] from 2001 to 2011.<ref name=currentprovost>[http://www.tcd.ie/provost/biog/ Current Provost's Biography]. Retrieved on 4 November 2009.{{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016004425/http://www.tcd.ie/provost/biog/ |date=16 October 2009 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
He was born in [[Claremorris]], [[County Mayo]], and was educated locally at [[St Colman's College, Claremorris|St Colman's College]]. He holds a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] in Physics/Chemistry/Mathematics/Philosophy from [[St Patrick's College, Maynooth]], a [[Higher Diploma|HDipEd]] also from Maynooth and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from [[NUI Galway|University College Galway]].<ref name=currentprovost/>

==Academic career==
Following a postdoctoral stay at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]], he was a research scientist at [[Bell Labs]], [[New Jersey]] for six years. He returned to Ireland in 1986 as a professor of Laser Physics at Trinity College. Producing over 140 publications, and developing several patents, he was a co-founder of Optronics Ireland and campus company Eblana Photonics. He is a member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]], the [[American Physical Society]], the [[Optical Society of America]], the [[IEEE|Institute of Electronic and Electrical Engineers]] and Fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref name=currentprovost/>

Before becoming Provost, Hegarty was Dean of Research and Head of the Physics Department.<ref name=currentprovost/>

==Personal life==
Hegarty is married to Neasa Ní Chinnéide, President of the [[European Bureau for Lesser-Used Languages]],<ref>"About Us" {{Cite web |url=http://www.eblul.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=14&Itemid=33 |title=EBLUL - European Bureau for Lesser-Used Languages - About Us |access-date=4 November 2009 |archive-date=1 December 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091201185012/http://www.eblul.org/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=14&Itemid=33 |url-status=bot: unknown }}. ''European Bureau for Lesser-Used Languages''. Retrieved on 4 November 2009.</ref> and they have two children, Cillian and Ciarán.<ref name=currentprovost/>
